column1: # Expected seconds per runner test file, for runner/test/run.sh --shard (lib/shard.mjs
# balances the shards with these). seconds<TAB>file.
# Source: CI run 41338925244 (main at cdff24e, 2026-11-01), every file's observed
# duration in all four cells (macOS node 22 and 24 at -j 3, ubuntu node 22 and 24 at
# -j 4), the MAXIMUM of the four passing runs, whole seconds, floor 1. The one failed
# run (parallel-stop.test.sh, macOS node 22: 125 s against 42-44 s elsewhere, repaired
# in 577c9e7) is left out. Max, not the macOS median: these numbers are also what
# run-harness.test.sh H10 holds against the caps, and a cap has to fit the slowest
# cell. The partition only uses the ratios, so the cell they came from barely matters.
# A test missing here counts 10s; a line for a deleted test is ignored.
# Refresh a line when a test gets much slower or faster (an off weight only unbalances
# the shards, it never drops or duplicates a test), and refresh the whole table from a
# green main run's logs now and then: every runner shard's log has one
# "::group::<file> — PASS (<n>s)" line per test.
# ESTIMATES until the next refresh (the test changed after that run):
#   delivery-lifecycle: 100 - 60, the two TICK_SLEEP=30 pauses it no longer sleeps (Linux alone: 95s -> 36s).
#   e2e-release-gate-merge-typecheck: 136 x 65/141, scenarios 1-2 only (Linux alone: 141s -> 65s).
#   direct-run-isolation: 224 x 16/213, the quick re-runs only (Linux alone: 213s -> 16s). It
#   stays in LONG_RE: the nightly GAFFER_TEST_EXHAUSTIVE=1 run re-runs all 16 tests (~220s).
#   land-tester-replay: 334 - 13, land-tester-replay-proof: 252 - 10, concurrency-bookkeeping: 67 - 12:
#   ticket setup in one node process (lib/wg-batch.mjs; setup alone 13.6s -> 0.3s, 10.7s -> 0.8s,
#   12.5s -> 0.3s on a loaded 4-CPU box). wg-batch-parity: new, 5s alone on Linux.
